tool_input.command: cd /tmp/run/demo-app; for f in app/*.py conftest.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat -n $f; done

result:
FINDING: app/auth.py:14 | SQL injection: `find_user` builds the query with an f-string from `name`. Use a parameterized query.
FINDING: app/auth.py:5 | Hardcoded signing secret in source. Load it from the environment or a secret store.
FINDING: app/auth.py:9 | The password salt is the username (`salt=name` at lines 21 and 30). It is predictable and not unique per user. Use a random per-user salt and store it.
FINDING: app/auth.py:33 | The token signs only `user_id`. It has no expiry, nonce or audience, so it can be replayed forever.
FINDING: app/files.py:10 | Path traversal in `export_report`: `filename` is not sanitized, so `../` or an absolute path writes outside the exports directory. `read_report` uses `basename`, but this function does not.
FINDING: app/orders.py:13 | Off-by-one: the docstring says $100.00 or more gets the discount, but `>` excludes exactly 10,000 cents. Use `>=`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:23 | Tax is computed on `subtotal`, but the docstring says it is charged on the discounted amount. Use `discounted`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:59 | `place_order` ignores the return value of `reserve`. The availability check and the reserve are not atomic, and each `reserve` commits on its own. A failure partway through, or a concurrent order, can leave stock partially reserved or oversold. A duplicate SKU in the cart can also pass the check twice but fail on reserve.
FINDING: app/orders.py:40 | `count_by_status` reads `order["status"]`, but the `orders` table has no `status` column (see `db.py:16`). It raises an error on real rows. It is also O(n·m); a single pass would do.
FINDING: app/orders.py:33 | `dedupe_skus` uses a list for the membership check, which is O(n²). Use a set alongside the list, or `dict.fromkeys`.
FINDING: app/orders.py:28 | `format_price` gives wrong output for negative cents (for example -150 gives "$-2.50").
FINDING: app/inventory.py:10 | Off-by-one in `paginate`: the slice ends at `start + page_size - 1`, so each page returns 9 items instead of 10. It also does not handle `page < 1`, which gives a negative start index.
FINDING: app/inventory.py:23 | `reserve` does a check-then-update without a transaction or an atomic `UPDATE ... WHERE qty >= ?`. This is a race condition. It also commits per call, which breaks the atomicity of `place_order`.
FINDING: app/db.py:37 | `INSERT OR REPLACE` in `add_item` silently overwrites an existing SKU row. There is no positional column list, so any schema change will break it.
